Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick intro at the end of last week. We're starting our intake for QuantumBank's platform assessments and have a few clarifying questions before we run the SIG/CAIQ and schedule a FedRAMP scoping call. I've attached our current CAIQ and SIG matrices (see filenames above). Can you confirm the following?

- What will Redwood define as the product boundary for ISO 27001 vs the FedRAMP authorization scope? (i.e., hosted API only, or also Dedicated/Private variants)
- Do you have snapshot/export capabilities for enclave images and environment metadata that auditors can consume? If so, what format and retention window?
- For log evidence we typically ask for 3 months of API call logs and 12 months of config-change history—can you provide that or an equivalent sample?
- Who are your named evidence owners for IAM, key management (KMS/HSM), and networking?
- Do you have SOC 2 Type II reports or a planned window for SOC 2 that overlaps this FedRAMP intake?

Goal: get a simple mutual action plan (owners + 2–3 week sample sprint) so our auditors can plan the intake and dry run.

We'd like to schedule a 30-minute intake call with owners on Wed/Thu next week (your timezone).

Thanks — Emily
Emily Torres
Head of Vendor Assurance
QuantumBank

Emily — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Copying Markus (infrastructure/security) and Grace (compliance program) to own the technical and program responses.

Quick answers up front:
- Boundary: by default we propose the hosted Redwood API surface as the primary authorization boundary. Dedicated and Private deployments can be scoped in as separate enclaves — we can document that mapping in the plan.
- Snapshots: we can produce environment manifests and container image digests. For Dedicated/Private we can include exported enclave manifests; format is JSON/CSV for metadata and tarballs for artifact bundles.
- Logs: we can export API call logs (JSON) and configuration change logs (CSV). We'll confirm retention windows but can provide 3 months of API logs and 12 months of config changes for the sample sprint.
- Evidence owners: Markus will own infra/KMS/networking artifacts; Grace will own policy/ISO narratives and evidentiary timelines. I'll own coordination and the mutual action plan.
- SOC 2: we have a Type II in-flight; our next rolling window completes in Q3 2026. We can share interim control narratives and prior reports where allowed.

Action proposal (MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_v1 attached):
1) Intake call — 30 min — proposed Thu 2026-02-19 10:00 PT (please confirm) — attendees: Emily, Alex, Mina, Markus, Grace.
2) Evidence sample sprint (2 weeks) — deliver sample bundles for 3 categories: IAM/KMS, Logging/Monitoring, Network/Boundary.
3) Dry run with auditors — schedule a 60-min walkthrough after sample delivery.

Open questions for your intake call: expected sample size per control, any required encryption proof artifacts (HSM certs), and whether your auditors need SBOMs or image attestations.

I'll attach a compact mutual action plan with owners and proposed dates.

- Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Compliance Engineering, Redwood Inference

Picking up on Mina's notes — tagging a few technical clarifications so expectations are aligned before the intake:

- Snapshots & artifacts: we can produce the following artifacts for the hosted API boundary:
  * environment_manifest.json (region, AZ mapping, instance types, kernel versions)
  * container_digest_list.csv (image:sha256, build timestamp)
  * kv_snapshot.tar (KV cache metadata, truncated) — note: we strip customer data.

- Logs: API call logs are stored in JSON line format in S3 for 180 days by default for hosted customers; we can export the last 90 days as requested. Config-change logs (Terraform/apply records + IAM policy diffs) are available for 12 months.

- KMS/HSM: we use customer-managed keys for Private deployments and AWS KMS for hosted; we can provide KMS key metadata and rotation records. We cannot export private key material (obviously) but can provide rotation and access logs.

- SBOMs & images: we publish SBOMs for our base runtime images and can produce image attestations for release tags used by your test tenancy. If auditors need provenance we can provide the attestation bundle.

Proposed owners & short timeline (internal):
  - Markus: infra artifacts export (due 2026-03-02)
  - Grace: control narratives & ISO mapping (due 2026-03-02)
  - Mina: coordinator/packaging & submission to QuantumBank (due 2026-03-04)

I'll prepare a small export playbook (commands, retention, redaction notes) and attach as 'REDWOOD_EXPORT_PLAYBOOK.md' in the upload.

On the intake call please confirm:
  1) exact controls auditors will probe first (so we prioritize exports),
  2) whether they require signed attestations, and
  3) sample size (e.g., 25 auth events per IAM control).

-- Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
